av_event.line_text: Marites: One, Rafael. He's nine. Every day he asks me for a little brother. I say, Rafael, who will look after the baby? You? And he says no.
av_event.what: Gemma's half-smile fades and she looks down at the table for about three seconds, lips pressed together, then looks back up at the screen and smiles again.

text:
B: Hello! Hi, can you hear me?
A: Hiya! Yes, I can hear you. I'm Gemma.
B: Marites. Sorry, my phone is on the rice cooker again, hehe.
A: Ha, that's fine. I'm propped up on a pile of cookbooks, so. How've your calls been?
B: Good! Everybody is nice. I just talked to Rob, the bird man. He says maybe he will come to Croydon to see the parakeets.
A: Oh, he's lovely, isn't he? I had him first. So what do you do, Marites?
B: I'm a carer, home care, in Croydon. I go to old people's houses and help them, washing, breakfast, medicine. Four days. And you?
A: I'm an upholsterer. So I recover old chairs, footstools, that kind of thing. I've got a little unit in Didcot.
B: Oh, that's nice! Like the TV programme, the sewing one?
A: Sewing Bee? I love that. It's sort of that, but with a staple gun. Some days I come home completely knackered from stapling and my hand's just like a claw.
B: Hehe. My back is like that. Lifting, bending, and then running for the bus.
A: Oh, I bet. Yours is proper hard work, though. Have you got kids?
B: One, Rafael. He's nine. Every day he asks me for a little brother. I say, Rafael, who will look after the baby? You? And he says no.
A: Ha, typical. I've got Isla, she's eight. She asks for a hamster mostly. Erm, I saw your cross in the photo, actually. Do you go to church?
B: Yes, every Sunday. Catholic. I'm always late, but I go.
A: I'm Church of England. Not every week any more, just Christmas, Easter, Isla's school services. But I do like it. It's quite calming, isn't it, just sitting there.
B: Yes, exactly. Calming. And after Mass, the Filipino group, we have food and chat. Now we are planning the Christmas party. Big karaoke.
A: Oh no, karaoke. I'd be hiding at the back.
B: No, you have to sing! I always sing the same song. Every year, same song, and everybody knows already.
A: Ha, what is it?
B: Erm, it's a Filipino love song. Very sad. Everybody cries, hehe.
A: Oh, I love that. Is there loads of food as well?
B: Oh my God, so much. I make pancit, a big tray. Always too much. Nobody goes home hungry.
A: That sounds amazing. I bake with Isla at the weekend, but the results are, erm, mixed. Last week the cupcakes sort of sank in the middle.
B: Hehe. Still you eat them, though?
A: Oh, we eat them. Every one. Rob had three.
B: And on my long shifts I eat Greggs. Sausage roll. Don't tell anybody.
A: Your secret's safe. Honestly, the Greggs by the station is the only reason I get through
